summary.text: Edward "Eddie" Gibbs represents New York's 68th Assembly District, which covers East Harlem, Randall's Island and parts of the Upper East Side and Central Harlem.
His official biography describes him as a community organizer and the first formerly incarcerated person to serve in the New York State Legislature.

paragraphs.text: Gibbs grew up in East Harlem with limited financial resources, according to his Assembly biography.
It says that at 17 he turned himself in after committing a crime, served time in prison, and returned to the community, and that he credits the experience with turning his life around.
He received an associate degree in business administration from Cayuga Community College.
The biography describes him as a community leader for over two decades who held annual coat drives, Thanksgiving dinners, toy giveaways and back-to-school supply drives.

During the COVID-19 pandemic it says he distributed food, water and protective equipment and helped older neighbors find vaccine appointments, and that he took water to Flint, Michigan, during its water crisis.
